content: Architecture-slicing (architecture_slice.slice_architecture) is telemetry-only for every scenario today, including implement — it is invoked only from inside context_budget.py and context_pack.py (imported), never as a live script, and no commands/dark-factory-*.md file consumes its sliced output; each command's Phase 1 does a literal full Read of ARCHITECTURE.md/CLAUDE.md. Only memory top-k (load_memory_context.sh -> memory_retrieve.py) and diff ranking (diff_rank.py) are genuinely live-consumed in agent prompts today. Don't assume architecture_md being in a scenario's _SECTION_REGISTRY means it changes what the agent sees; check for an actual reviewer-prompt/command consumer before claiming a live effect.

Rejected adding a 'comment digest' section for conformance/code-review's token-optimization routing (issue #19): comment_digest.py is purpose-built around the factory-boundary-marker/continue-intent re-run cadence with no home in single-pass gates, neither scenario loads issue-comment content today (no existing baseline to optimize), and injecting raw comments into conformance specifically risks re-surfacing scope the spec deliberately excluded (fights its scope-enforcement mandate). Chosen instead: extend _SECTION_REGISTRY with architecture_md (telemetry/eval parity only) + memory_context (made genuinely live via the pre-provisioned validate/review PHASE_SOURCE_MAP keys in memory_retrieve.py).

Rejected expanding issue #19's scope to build Factory CPM / cost-saved / quality-signal / failure-spend tracking directly inside conformance/code-review token-optimization routing, despite a later issue comment (citing an external harness-economics paper) requesting it. Verified the referenced epic (#234, Harness economics) directly: its own backlog table scopes #19's contribution as 'phase-specific savings measurement' only (i.e. evals/token_opt_eval.py's per-scenario savings_pct), with CPM/quality/failure-spend synthesis assigned to #234's own child issues, and its Non-Goals explicitly forbid duplicating the raw ledger. Run-level Factory CPM/retry-spend/failure-spend already exist at factory_core/run_record.py (~line 522) and factory_core/cost_report.py (~line 92) -- building a scenario-scoped copy inside #19 would duplicate that machinery. When a spec-revision comment cites an external paper/epic to argue for scope expansion, check whether the cited epic itself already scopes the current ticket narrowly before expanding -- the epic's own backlog decomposition is more authoritative than a comment's framing.
